The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d179fa55e4b82fed), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 14-15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: Let Bh be the critical mass of strict bridges of height h from one fixed port, and let B0 = 1. Then Bh ≍ (1 + h)−1/4. For sufficiently large fixed T, bridges confined to transverse width Th have mass at least cT h−1/4 and first-length mass at most CT h13/12. The arch-plus-bridge mass in a height-h strip with diameter larger than r ≥ Ch is at most Ch−1/4e−cr/h. Since a self-avoiding path of diameter r has at most Cr2 centers, this estimate also controls every fixed length moment in the tail. In particular the mass at D > h log2 h, including any fixed length power, is smaller than every inverse power of h. The half-plane arch mass at prescribed horizontal gap g satisfies Ag ≍ g−5/4; its lower bound remains valid with diameter at most Cg for a sufficiently large fixed C. The normalized irreducible law satisfies 1 − Epe−tH ≍ t3/4 (0 < t ≤ 1), p(D > r) ≤ Cr−3/4 (r ≥ 1). For h large, put R0 = h(log h)1/64 and l− = h4/3 (log h)−1/8 , l+ = h4/3 (log h)1/2 . 14 For a fixed finite C, ∑︂ j≤2R0 Bj{l− ≤ L ≤ 2l+} ≥ h3/4 (log h)−C . (2) The estimate sums over heights and terminal ports; it does not prescribe either one of them.
